messages:
maria: quick flag — noticed a p50 bump (~12%) on host ingress after the preparse change in canary earlier. correlates with more CPU in parselet::dispatch and grpc::writev
aj: saw that too. p50 went from 18ms -> 20.2ms on small chat workloads.
devon: what changed in preparse? i thought we only toggled 'multiplex_smallframes' to true.
maria: yep. the change increased the windowing heuristic which lets more microframes flow to tokenization before coalescing. good for throughput but looks like it ups host-side overhead for short requests.
kai: stack sample from the canary host: ```
+ 34% parselet::dispatch
+ 22% token::tokenize_chunk
+ 14% grpc::writev
+ 10% kvcache::lookup
```
aj: grpc::writev at 14% is notable — if we emit more small writes due to microframes we pay syscalls.
devon: KV cache at 10% suggests more prefix misses? or more small lookups per request. any kvcache hit-rate diff?
maria: hit-rate down ~2.5% on the canary cohort. i think the batching heuristics end up splitting prefixes across frames, so cache keys not reused as before.
ingress-bot: deploy-canary: canary rollout 40% -> 60% at 2026-03-19T11:02Z
aj: repro cmd: ```bash
wrk -t8 -c50 -d30s -s scripts/sim-chat.lua --small-reqs
```
maria: quick triage notes:
- hypothesis A: multiplex_smallframes increases syscall writev frequency -> syscall overhead on hot hosts
- hypothesis B: increased microframe boundary breaks common prefix patterns -> kvcache churn
- hypothesis C: kernel selection changed for some models (fallback to generic kernel on 1p shard) exposing extra CPU in tokenization path
devon: i profiled kernels on the same canary host — some requests used fallback kernels due to sequence_len heuristics mismatch. fallback cost +8% on tokenization stage.
kai: short-term mitigation options:
- revert multiplex_smallframes for small-request route (fast rollback)
- coalesce at ingress earlier (host-side writev batching)
- increase kvcache normalization window to avoid split keys
- pin kernel selection for the canary models to avoid fallback path
aj: i can try a parameter tweak: force host writev batch threshold from 256B -> 1KB for small-req route and run canary again. low risk.
maria: devon, can you drop a flame with full call stacks and kvcache keys for a few sample requests? pastetop to thread.
devon: on it — grabbing 10 samples. also attaching a short log snippet: ```
[2026-03-19T11:10:02Z] req=abcd tokenized=78 cpu_ms=21 parselet=7 token=9 writev=3 kvcache_hit=false
[2026-03-19T11:10:03Z] req=efgh tokenized=65 cpu_ms=19 parselet=6 token=8 writev=4 kvcache_hit=true
```
aj: if writev variance is high we should consider a micro-coalesce layer in proxy that aggregates writes per-connection up to 1ms or X bytes. saves syscalls and keeps streaming latency low.
kai: longer term: revisit batching heuristic — adapt window by request size distribution instead of fixed toggle. tune kernel selection mapping based on seq_len histogram from trace.
maria: ok action items:
- aj: try writev threshold tweak and run another 30m canary (low risk)
- devon: upload the 10 flame samples + kvcache keys by EOD
- kai: draft a config change for kvcache normalization/windowing (small delta)
- maria: hold rollback plan ready if p50 stays up after tweaks

maria: one more note — we should add a quick eval to the canary checks: p50 tokenization and writev syscalls per-request. current canary only checks overall p50 which hides these host-side shifts.
aj: agreed. will add metrics in the canary dashboard. :thumbsup:
devon: uploaded samples to /tmp/canary-flames-181999 (will move to s3 after triage)
maria: thanks team. i'll update this thread with canary results. staying oncall for the next hour.
ingress-bot: deploy-canary: canary scaled back to 30% at 2026-03-19T11:34Z (rollback not initiated)
maria: update (11:45) — aj's writev tweak at 11:22 reduced writev cost from 14% -> 6% in samples. p50 back to 18.6ms. continuing monitor.
aj: leaving the tweak enabled in canary, rolling to 50% over next 20m.
maria: moving to post-triage doc once stable. thanks.
